scores.evidence: M1 shadow slice + spikes → M2 inline rules → M3 ML (Depends on: Spike B data. M1 `libs/features`. M2 labels.) → M4 alerts
scores.rationale: Substrate (infra, features, contract, lake) precedes enforcement, which precedes the model, with explicit dependencies and spikes proving unknowns first.

scores.evidence: The Decision Service receives 100% of production authorisations in shadow mode, with no effect on cardholders.
scores.rationale: M1 is a real end-to-end production slice (service, Redis, Kafka, lake, pipeline deploy) before enforcement or the model.

scores.evidence: D2 Fail open ... Revisit if: Losses during outages become material. Then: fail closed only for high-risk merchant categories.
scores.rationale: Decisions D0–D11 and A1–A14 list options, reversibility, defaults and explicit flip conditions.

scores.evidence: T1–T3 on day 1–2 (long-lead requests, contract, Spike C), then infra/CI/features before rules and leaf items; M2 'Guardrail' before enforcement
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (contract, infra, shared feature lib, guardrails, rollback) are ordered before leaf work such as alerts and UI.

scores.evidence: Threats tagged (M1), (M1–M2), (M2): mTLS, Secrets Manager rotation (M1), Trivy in CI, no-PAN contract, Luhn scrubber
scores.rationale: Security is concrete from M1 (mTLS, IAM, secrets, scanning, PAN controls) and continues through M2 to M4 (Lake Formation, allow-window approvals).

scores.evidence: Observability (M1, extended each milestone) ... T14 OTel metrics and traces ... 'Decision health' dashboard
scores.rationale: Metrics, traces, dashboards are built in M1 and extended in each later milestone with paging, fraud performance and drift monitoring.

scores.evidence: Terraform ... No manual console changes; immutable rulesets/<git-sha>.json with SHA-256; replay through same feature code; signed images
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is threaded via IaC, signed images, immutable versioned configs/models, manifests, and replay parity across milestones.

scores.evidence: With Kafka down, `Score` still answers and the drop metric increments; Redis failover under load; Redis rebuild < 30 min tested
scores.rationale: Failure handling (timeouts, degraded modes, fail-open, rebuild, DLQ, chaos drills) appears from M1 and in each subsequent phase.

scores.evidence: Evaluation first: a versioned evaluation set exists in M1 ... Guardrails: fire-rate cap with auto-revert ... Shadow before enforcement
scores.rationale: For a classical ML system, guardrails, shadow, human-approved promotion and fallback precede the model; retrieval/memory/orchestration layers are N/A and feedback (labels, retrain) comes last, though AI concerns sit partly in a cross-cutting section.

scores.evidence: Stream processor (Flink) ... Trigger to build it: A specific feature with proven lift ... or Redis CPU > 60%
scores.rationale: A deferred-work table gives each item an explicit pull-forward trigger, plus non-goals and deliberate shortcuts.

note: Exceptionally thorough plan with a shadow-mode production slice first, explicit decision flips, and threaded security, observability and resilience; only minor weakness is AI-layer discipline being described in a cross-cutting section.
